tasks.short: Plan and lead group recreation activities

steps.what: Plan and organize group activities around customer needs and available resources
Lead group activities and adapt to participants and actual conditions

tasks.design: Keep activity selection, practical organisation and group leadership with the manager. Existing activity guidance in {DOCS} supports the plan without replacing participant judgement or physical delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: A workable group activity depends on interests, conditions and available resources.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing guidance can support planning; no replacement for facilitation is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Choose an inclusive activity and adjust it as participants respond.
tasks.human_edge: Notice discomfort, confusion or unsafe participation and intervene appropriately.
tasks.altitude: Activity planning and leadership responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Recognise participation limits and make practical adjustments.

evidence.claim: Group facilitation and contextual activity planning remain human work; a scheduling capability does not establish savings in leading an activity.

assumptions: Boundary is session planning, organisation and leadership, excluding facility-wide programming strategy and separate staff scheduling.

The manager gathers interests and checks resources in s1; no structured participant suitability or equipment-ready flag is presumed. Participants produce responses during s2 after the activity begins.
Existing participant involvement remains unchanged outside the focal denominator. Native document access suffices; no new tool, capture duty or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Activity types and manager's delivery duties
research_questions: Which practical constraints most often require a change to a planned group activity?

already_counted.description: All contextual planning, organisation and leadership remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+60=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Neither activity planning judgement nor physical leadership is reduced.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train workers in company procedures and policy

steps.what: Train workers by explaining company procedures and policy with practical examples
Observe workers applying procedures and correct misunderstandings through coaching

tasks.design: Use current procedures in {DOCS} while the manager explains and demonstrates their application. Keep observation, questions and corrective coaching human; document access alone does not establish competence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workers must understand and apply a procedure rather than merely receive it.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing policy access supports the training conversation without replacing coaching.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise misunderstandings and adapt the explanation to actual work.
tasks.human_edge: Check demonstrated understanding and explain why a procedure matters.
tasks.altitude: Training and coaching responsibilities stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Use practical examples and teach-back to check understanding.

evidence.claim: Practical training includes explanation and checking actual application; access to a policy library does not replace those activities.

assumptions: Boundary is direct training and coaching, excluding policy authorship, course production and attendance reporting.

The policy owner supplies current approved procedures before s1. Workers produce practice attempts after s1 and before or during s2; the manager observes them in retained s2 time, with no free comprehension flag.
Existing learner time remains unchanged outside the focal denominator. Native document access suffices; no new system, recording or upkeep is proposed, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Which procedures are misunderstood despite clear written guidance?

already_counted.description: Explanation, observation and corrective coaching remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+55=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Direct training time is retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write and present recreational programming strategies

steps.what: Evaluate customer or employee data and choose the recreational facility programming strategy
Write the strategy and presentation from the manager's chosen recommendations

loop.purpose: Draft a clear account of the manager's strategy and evidence.
loop.input: Checked brief with selected recommendations, source figures, limitations and audience.
loop.output: Strategy draft and presentation text linked to brief evidence.
loop.check: Manager verifies every recommendation, number and rationale against the brief and checks that descriptive data is not presented as causal proof or a statement about individual staff.
loop.stop: At most two redrafts; unsupported rationale or poor fidelity returns to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native templates provide structure but cannot write a coherent explanation of varied recommendations and caveats.

steps.what: Verify and present strategies and discuss trade-offs with the decision makers

tasks.design: Use existing {BI} outputs to inform the manager's strategy choice, then a bounded loop in {DOCS} drafts its explanation. The manager checks the draft and approves the exact version before presenting it; implementation authority remains in the existing decision process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing a clear argument takes time after the manager has chosen a course of action.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can express an already selected strategy while preserving evidence references.
tasks.still_hard: Choose meaningful programming priorities and balance conflicting customer, staff and resource needs.
tasks.human_edge: Make and defend the trade-offs rather than treating historical demand as a complete strategy.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft writing; strategy choice and presentation remain the manager's responsibility.

reach.learn: Distinguish evidence, assumptions and resource trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Bounded drafting can help explain a manager-selected strategy; the proposed design and saving are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is strategy evaluation, writing and presentation, excluding new surveys, individual worker assessment, bookings and implementation.
Existing booking and authorised feedback owners supply current aggregate customer or employee data before s1 through unchanged reporting work. No new data collection is presumed.

The manager captures source versions, period, measures, aggregation level, limitations, chosen recommendations, rationale, constraints and audience in retained s1 time. Missing or unreliable data requires manual clarification, not a free structured strategy input.
The loop uses only the checked brief. Draft review stays in s2 and final presentation checking stays in s3. Individual staff profiling is outside scope.
Test native report and presentation templates first. Incremental focal upkeep for drafting instructions and source checks is 6 hours per 100 baseline hours.
unknowns: Quality and authorised use of existing data
research_questions: Can a brief-based draft preserve the manager's actual trade-offs without increasing final review time?

already_counted.description: Evidence interpretation and strategy choice remain.
Draft verification and correction remain in writing time.
Final checking, presentation and discussion remain.

incremental.description: Maintain drafting guidance and investigate source-reference errors.

approvals.approved_version: Exact strategy and presentation versions, figures, recommendations and audience approved before presentation in s3; any change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+40*0.65+25=86; gross=14, upkeep=6, central net=8. Conservative 0-4 allows substantial rewriting and weak source data; strategy decisions and presentation retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Store and retrieve equipment safely, checking identity, condition and storage location

tasks.design: Keep physical equipment storage and retrieval with the responsible manager. Existing storage guidance in {DOCS} may identify locations, but no record is treated as proof of actual location or safe condition.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment must be located, handled and physically checked.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing location guidance supports the work without performing it.
tasks.still_hard: Handle varied equipment safely and recognise damage or unsuitable storage.
tasks.human_edge: See the actual equipment condition and stop unsafe handling.

reach.learn: Use designated locations and recognise handling restrictions.

evidence.claim: A storage record does not physically move equipment or establish its present condition.

assumptions: Boundary is physical storing and retrieval, excluding repair, procurement and separate inventory reporting.
Requesters supply the equipment need before s1; the manager identifies location and observes condition during retained s1 time. No free structured location, readiness or condition flag is assumed.
Native guidance is sufficient if already available. No new tracking application or capture obligation is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Which storage arrangements cause avoidable physical searching or unsafe handling?

already_counted.description: All locating, handling and checking remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No physical movement or checking is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The manager retains direct service, training, physical handling and strategy decisions; only first-draft strategy writing receives a modest conditional saving.
reach: Share practical activity and training methods with wellness coordinators.
role.ambitious_version: Use any released writing time to discuss practical programming choices with customers and staff.
